blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
For British clients, trust is built slowly. They rarely sign a big contract at the first meeting. First, they watch how you behave over time. Do you deliver? Are you on time? Do you admit small mistakes quickly?

For the first few months, expect polite interest and careful questions, not warm enthusiasm. This is not coolness. It is how the British test a new partner.

Once trust is earned, British clients are loyal for a very long time. Patience at the start is rewarded for years.

items.q: How do British clients build trust?
options: By being very warm at first
By signing a big contract fast
items.why: "trust is built slowly" — a confiança se constrói devagar, com o tempo.

items.q: What do British clients do at the first meeting?
options: They rarely sign a big contract
items.why: "They rarely sign a big contract at the first meeting."

items.q: What does the text say about polite interest and careful questions?
options: They mean the deal is closed
They are how the British test a new partner
They are a sign of coolness
They mean the client is angry
items.why: "It is how the British test a new partner."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Patience at the start can be rewarded
British clients can be loyal for years
Careful questions mean the British client is not interested
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que as perguntas são um teste, não frieza nem falta de interesse.

items.q: "Patience at the start is rewarded for years" suggests that…
options: A patient partner can win a long, loyal relationship
The first meeting is the most important
items.why: Inferência: esperar no começo traz uma relação longa e leal depois.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James falando com um colega novo de vendas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Don't worry. I know the client is still asking small questions after three meetings. That is normal here. British clients are like this.

They do not sign a big contract fast. First, they watch us. They want to see if we deliver. They want to see if we are on time. They want to see if we admit small mistakes quickly.

So please, do not push too hard. Do not promise big things. Just do your job well, every week. Answer their questions in a calm and polite way.

Right now they show polite interest, not warm enthusiasm. That is a good sign, not a bad one. It means they are testing us. This is how they build trust.

If we are patient and we deliver, they will trust us. And when a British client trusts you, they stay loyal for many years. So be patient. The wait is worth it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is the client still asking small questions after three meetings?
options: It is normal — British clients are like this
The colleague made a big mistake
items.why: "That is normal here. British clients are like this."

items.q: What does James tell the new colleague to do?
options: Push hard and promise big things
Do the job well every week and answer questions politely
items.why: "Just do your job well, every week. Answer their questions in a calm and polite way."

items.q: According to James, polite interest is…
options: a sign the client is bored
a good sign — they are testing us
a sign the deal is lost
items.why: "That is a good sign, not a bad one. It means they are testing us."

items.q: Why does James say "do not push too hard"?
options: Because the contract is too small
Because pushing hard can break the slow trust the British need
items.why: Inferência: a confiança britânica é lenta, então pressionar demais atrapalha.

items.q: What does James suggest will happen if they are patient and deliver?
options: The client will trust them and stay loyal for years
The client will ask for a lower price
items.why: Inferência: "when a British client trusts you, they stay loyal for many years."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We need to build trust with this new client." To build trust means to…
options: make the client trust you over time
items.why: Build trust = construir confiança, aos poucos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We always ___ our reports on time, so the client is happy."
items.why: Deliver = entregar / cumprir no prazo.

items.q: "She kept her promise and finished the work." A promise is…
options: something you say you will do
items.why: Promise = promessa: algo que você diz que vai fazer.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The client asks careful questions to ___ if we are a good partner."
items.why: Test = testar: é o que o cliente britânico faz com um novo parceiro.

items.q: "Good clients stay loyal for many years." Loyal means…
items.why: Loyal = fiel: o cliente permanece com você por muito tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em negócios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the deal." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new service next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = lançar, colocar em prática.

items.q: "Two clients pushed back on the price." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "We made a promise, so now we must follow through." To follow through means to…
options: do what you said you would do
items.why: Follow through = cumprir, levar até o fim o combinado.

items.q: "Let's keep in touch after the meeting." To keep in touch means to…
items.why: Keep in touch = manter contato.
